A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TypedThinker work despite the revised title. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, reasoning-diversity measurements and transfer experiments, including results for GPT-4o and MetaMath.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Qwen 2, LiveBench, Self-Discover comparisons, repeated-run component studies and ContextHub subgroup results.

M1.justification: The meta-thinker, type-specific retrieval, reasoner fine-tuning, correctness and reasoning-type filtering, and greedy or weighted aggregation remain unchanged. Recasting explicit memory as a demonstration collection and correcting example labels do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds three LiveBench reasoning tasks: spatial, web of lies v2 and zebra puzzle. This extends coverage within the existing reasoning domain. The new ContextHub abstract-category results disaggregate previously evaluated coverage; the commonsense example comes from the retained LogiQA dataset.

E2.justification: Self-Discover joins the retained comparison methods in Tables 1 and 4, with single-response and self-consistency results in Table 1. The new appendix ablations also compare base LLMs augmented only with the meta-thinker or demonstration collection. The existing comparator set is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: New experimental configurations include Qwen 2-7B-Instruct, a 70/30 LiveBench split and add-one-component controls. Existing benchmark splits, evaluation metrics, decoding settings and training budgets remain unchanged. The training details move from Section 4.1 to Appendix A.3; revised LLaMA3 scores do not establish an underlying protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5.3 substantially extends component attribution beyond v1's Mistral-only removal ablation by testing base LLM plus meta-thinker and base LLM plus collection across both Mistral and LLaMA3 (Tables 13-14). Appendix A.6 additionally examines performance specifically on ContextHub's abstract symbolic problems (Table 15).

E5.justification: Tables 13-14 newly report means and standard deviations from three repetitions. This adds uncertainty reporting for the component studies, while the main accuracy tables remain point estimates. The existing Kendall correlation p-value reporting is retained; no seed identities or paper-wide increase in runs are established.

E6.justification: LLaMA3 results change substantially in Tables 1, 3 and 4 without an explanation of the revisions. In Table 1, few-shot+SC average accuracy changes from 0.382 to 0.497, while TypedThinker+SC changes from 0.549 to 0.562. v2 also adds Qwen, Self-Discover, LiveBench, component and subgroup results. Table 10's reduced decimal precision is equivalent rounding, not a result change.

T1.justification: The effectiveness-score and effective-set definitions, retrieval condition and pairwise diversity formula remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version presents theorems or proofs, and the additional discussion does not introduce new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the reported LLaMA3 average-accuracy gain from 16.7 to 6.5 percentage points and add a roughly 7-point Qwen 2 gain. The central claims about reasoning diversification, type selection and transfer remain intact. MetaMath receives greater prominence but was already evaluated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for Self-Discover's difficulties and explicitly acknowledges the fine-tuning confound in comparisons with few-shot baselines. Appendix A.6 discusses symbolic and commonsense applicability, missing commonsense annotations and the possible need for task-specific demonstrations or light fine-tuning in distant domains. The original single-reasoning-type limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents Self-Discover's implementation and task-level structure construction, expands dataset descriptions, and corrects the swapped abductive and analogical examples in v1 Table 11, now Table 16. The explicit ThinkHub code URL disappears, although generic code/data-release language remains. Existing hardware and fine-tuning hyperparameters are relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: Related work gains discussion of inductive reasoning approaches, multi-agent diversity and meta-prompting, alongside references supporting Self-Discover and the added evaluations. The introduction drops the explicit weak-to-strong-generalization connection and Burns citation. These refine the positioning while preserving the central distinction of selecting suitable reasoning types for individual problems.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are rewritten, and the method description repeatedly replaces memory terminology with demonstration-collection language. Training details move into the appendix, which is reorganized into dataset descriptions/examples, training, analyses, additional experiments and applicability discussion. The title, affiliation text and conference header also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from stacked to grouped bars with percentage-axis labels. The method diagrams are relabeled and relocated, existing comparison tables gain rows, and five new result tables plus boxed dataset examples substantially expand the displays. The original reasoning-example table is retained as Table 16 with corrected example assignments.

improvement.justification: The added external baseline, Qwen/LiveBench evaluations and repeated-run component studies provide useful empirical checks absent in v1, while corrected reasoning examples improve reproducibility. These yield a modest net gain, limited by removal of the direct code URL and unresolved reporting inconsistencies: v2 Table 1 gives LLaMA3 few-shot GSM8K accuracy as 0.581, versus 0.476 ± 0.004 in Table 14 without a stated setting distinction.
